text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated GPU pool 'acme-dedicated-1' (us-east-1) exhausted for tenant AcmeCorp. 99% GPU utilization across nodes, request queue > 1200, 503s increasing. Trigger: pool_capacity_threshold.

maya (oncall): acked. pulling metrics now. paging me if customer impact observed.

sam (sre): seeing huge spike in prefix requests to ttr-generation model from AcmeCorp - looks like a batch replay. Q length per-node: 300+. OOMs 12 in last 5m.

leo (infra): confirmed dedicated pool can't autoscale beyond reserved nodes automatically. there is burst-to-shared option but needs manual approval (cost + throttling risk).

maya (oncall): tagging product and pm for decision: @priya @olivia we need go/no-go on burst. if we don't act, requests will drop with ~30% 503s within 10m.

priya (acct): looping in Acme PM now, trying to confirm whether this is expected traffic. sending message.

alex (cust-success): FYI Acme's contact is on call but might be asleep (APAC). i pinged account SLACK and email.

priya (acct): message to customer: "Hey @acme-oncall we're seeing a big spike from your dedicated pool causing failures. We're evaluating options (burst to shared or throttle). Can you confirm any planned load?"

olivia (eng-runtime): quick note: if we burst to shared-high-priority, we can sustain load but quality routing might route to quantized variants; not ideal but keeps throughput. Also need to flip routing for Acme tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.

maya (oncall): steps i'm running now: `rctl pool describe acme-dedicated-1` and `rctl pool tasks list --pool acme-dedicated-1 --since 5m`

sam (sre): logs snippet from node-gpu-7:
```
E 17:34:21 kernel: out-of-memory killer invoked
WARN model_runner: evicting KV cache for stream 0x7f9
ERROR api: backend returned 503 connection reset
```

leo (infra): capacity table: reserved nodes=8, active nodes=8, queued autoscale requests=0. shared-high has spare capacity 24 gpus but flagged for burst use. cost estimate for 1h burst ~ $2.1k.

maya (oncall): customer hasn't confirmed. we need to decide within 8-10m. options: 1) Burst to shared-high (manual) 2) Throttle Acme to X rps (fast) 3) Route Acme to another region (latency) 4) Temporarily enable graceful degradation (reduce tokens)

priya (acct): Acme replied: "not expected, we're running a large A/B replay. we can pause if needed but must not lose jobs. can you protect in place?"

alex (cust-success): they're willing to pause the replay if it avoids cross-tenant impact. asking for 5-10m to coordinate.

olivia (eng-runtime): on mitigation: we can enable tenant-level throttling per-route in the control plane with `rbac/tenant-quota set acme 250rps` — takes ~30s to apply. that will preserve core latency for other tenants.

sam (sre): i'd prefer throttling first, then burst if customer refuses to pause. throttling reduces 503s for others fast.

maya (oncall): initiating throttling to 200 rps now. command: `redwood ctl quota set --tenant acme --rps 200`

incident-bot: ACTION: quota change applied by maya (oncall) at 17:40:02 UTC. New tenant quota: 200 rps.

sam (sre): queue dropped to ~400 total, GPU OOMs decreased. error rate to other tenants back to normal. still some 503s for Acme's jobs.

priya (acct): customer confirms they've paused replay. they're asking us to hold burst for now and resume only if necessary.

leo (infra): recommend no burst now. keep throttling and monitor for 30m. if queue rebuilds, escalate to burst + commit to cost-owner signoff.

olivia (eng-runtime): we'll also enable prefix cache bypass for Acme so repeated prefixes don't rehydrate KV cache and pressure GPU memory. command: `rctl tenant config set acme kv_cache_mode=read_only` — applying.

maya (oncall): applying read_only mode.

incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: kv_cache_mode=read_only applied to tenant 'acme' by maya at 17:44:10 UTC.

sam (sre): monitoring metrics: GPU util -> 78% within 6m, queue -> 120, 503s drop to 15%. much better.

priya (acct): Acme says they'll re-run in 30m and wants a contact if things degrade. asked for a scheduled burst window next week.

olivia (eng-runtime): action items: 1) keep throttling for 30m 2) keep kv_cache read_only 3) if fail -> manual burst to shared-high for up to 1h with signoff 4) schedule follow-up with Acme to discuss replay controls and cost implications

maya (oncall): handing off to @sam for next 4hr watch. my shift starts ending. sam are you taking?

sam (sre): taking handoff. i'll maintain watch and escalate if metrics degrade.

maya (oncall): thanks — documented incident in postmortem backlog with tag `customer-dedicated-exhaustion` and provisional Sev: S2 (tenant-impacting but mitigated).

priya (acct): i'll set up a customer call in next 2 hours to review replay controls and request a committed burst slot if they need it.

leo (infra): noted cost + billing owner — if we ever do burst, route billing to enterprise-billing-acct and send invoice for out-of-plan usage.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: escalation silenced at 17:48:01 UTC; oncall transfer to sam (sre).

sam (sre): monitoring continues. leaving this thread open until stable for 30m. final status note will be added after watch. :thumbsup:
